messages:
Sana Ahmed: Hey — got a support ticket where the Python quickstart failed during auth. The README tells users to set REDWOOD_API_TOKEN but our SDK reads REDWOOD_API_KEY. New users were getting `401 Unauthorized` silently and then retrying manually.

Julian Park: Oof. Did they paste the example from the README verbatim?

Sana Ahmed: Yep. README snippet:```py
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_TOKEN'))
```

Maya Chen: Two issues there: env var name mismatch (REDWOOD_API_TOKEN vs REDWOOD_API_KEY) and the sample uses the old blocking client that doesn't enable our recommended retry/backoff wrapper. We now ship `create_client` which wires retries and introspects tokens. Correct example should be:
```py
import os
from redwood import create_client
client = create_client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
```

Maya Chen: Proposed fixes: 1) Update README to use REDWOOD_API_KEY; 2) change sample to `create_client` (adds retries by default); 3) add a one-line troubleshooting FAQ about 401s caused by wrong env var; 4) add a tiny CI smoke test that runs the Python quickstart with a fake token to verify error messages are actionable.

Julian Park: Also add a short note in the sample about how the client exposes `.retry_policy` config so advanced users can tune backoff for flaky networks. We've had a couple of customers confuse our global SDK-level retries with per-request retry headers.

doc-bot: Created docs issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/702 "python quickstart: env var name + create_client + retry note"

ops-bot: FYI we saw a spike of 5xxs from the demo region yesterday; might be worth linking the retry guidance to region failover docs.

Sana Ahmed: Thanks — I'll open the PR with README changes and FAQ. I'll include a tiny unit that runs the quickstart in CI and asserts the 401 message says "check REDWOOD_API_KEY".

Maya Chen: Sounds good. Ping me for review.
